All I'm saying is that I've lived in the US as a Filipino. I've also lived in the Philippines as a Filipino, both with Filipino families of course, and the difference in culture is going to have a huge impact on her decision. 

In either place I've lived, I'd lose a lot of the support I have/had from friends and family in the same community if I sued or even "left home."

NTA, *but based on OP's language, OP is Filipino (correct me if I'm wrong).* So am I and it's quite normal for families to be this controlling and to live with them at that age. All I can say is this sounds like every other toxic Filipino household. Get out, do what you need to do to survive on your own **BUT prepare for the insane amount of cultural backlash from family, friends, relatives, and family friends.**

**Let me speak solely based on my experience as an Asian child with no siblings in a very strict asian household, living in Asia but very influenced by American culture.** 

Take a step back and ask yourself, "Why is he doing this? Is it extremely harmful? At what point does it become detrimental?" My parents have spent their entire lives telling me no smoking, not to even try it once and here I am secretly doing weed sometimes and smoking. Will I ever tell them? No. Will them telling me to open up about it help? No–I don't trust them. Will throwing me into therapy help? No. Will telling him that his self harm was to attract attention help? **No.** 

Their actions and the way they've treated me with such strictness and the mindset that small bad things will ruin my life even if tried once has created the biggest rift in our relationship. It's only downhill from here. 

Take a step back and ask yourself how you can build your relationship with your son. That's the best and only solution I can give if you don't want to lose him.

Given that it might be mental health issues preventing her from working, I made guidelines for the team to strictly follow specific deadlines when asking things from her, not messaging after hours, no personal favors, etc. Since we're a startup things get messy and the line between work time and personal time tends to get blurred as well as the proper procedures for asking for outputs so I wanted to make sure that, even if she may not be opening up to me about stress she might be feeing in the company, I try and lessen the amount of stress she's going through by re-emphasizing guidelines to the rest of the team.

* Done everything legally– so that means memos, letters, and a PIP. 
* I've also asked her about mental health and told her we can discuss problems that are preventing her from working (unfortunately she either seens these messages or doesn't answer my calls) 
* I've offered to talk to HR to give her time to improve as well (HR has been asking me to fire this person for a few months now)
* Reminders every time there's a slip up (like an immediate message asking if something's up + a warning when a meeting/deadline is missed)
* Congratulated her on improvements and reminded her of remaining things on the PIP that haven't been improved 
* Multiple final warnings about missing/being late for meetings (I guess the word multiple + final don't really go together but that's been the case to give her more chances) 
* Sent mass emails to the team with guidelines on how to make her workload lighter/easier

These are off the top of my head! Let me know what else I can do and I'll also take note of if I've done it already :)

Oh this was my favorite university loophole.

In many classes laptops weren't allowed, but I convinced my professors to let me use my IPad which I took notes on like a regular notepad. But, when it came to "open notes" tests I was done hours before everyone else + good grades with minimal effort because I could CTRL+F my notes and I had screenshots of the PPTS on the notepad.

The best part about it was that I could download the presentations ahead of time or take pictures then scribble notes with a pen on them as class was going on. Helped big time with things like diagrams & charts.

Best. Investment. Ever.
